prospects.thesis: SMCI is the leading AI server integrator with direct exposure to Blackwell/Rubin GPU deployment cycles, and the P/S of 0.7x is remarkably cheap for a company with hyperscaler and enterprise AI infrastructure tailwinds. The 45% monthly move signals momentum re-acceleration post-accounting overhang, while bullish options and institutional flow confirm smart-money accumulation. Liquid-cooled rack-scale systems remain a differentiated moat as AI datacenter power density scales.

Leidos combines defense IT modernization, cyber, and health contract wins with a very reasonable 1.0x P/S, offering GARP exposure to rising DoD digital/AI budgets. The 32.6% monthly rally reflects backlog momentum and margin expansion in the Digital Modernization segment, while bullish institutional flow supports continuation. Entry now captures FY26 budget appropriations tailwinds and AI-in-government spending.

Kratos is a pure-play on unmanned systems, tactical drones, and hypersonics — the highest-growth pockets of defense spending under the Replicator initiative and CCA program. Distinct from LDOS (services) and HII (shipbuilding), KTOS captures the autonomous-weapons sub-niche where CCA jet contracts could compound revenue. Bullish options and institutional positioning ahead of Q3 program milestones make current momentum extendable.

MongoDB's document database is emerging as a preferred vector store for generative AI applications, with Atlas Vector Search driving reacceleration in consumption revenue. The 35.7% monthly rally reflects a fundamental inflection as enterprise AI workloads move from POC to production, and bullish institutional flow signals conviction into the September earnings print. Distinct AI infrastructure sub-niche vs. compute-focused names.

UiPath is pivoting from classic RPA to agentic AI automation, and at 5.0x P/S with an $8.4B cap it offers asymmetric upside if the AI-agent narrative sustains enterprise ARR growth. The 35% monthly move plus bullish options/institutional signals suggest a re-rating is underway ahead of the September earnings catalyst. Different sub-niche (application-layer agents) from MDB's data-layer play, preserving portfolio diversity.

market_pulse.rotation_analysis: Big money is piling into Real Estate in a way that's hard to ignore — a put/call ratio of 0.12 with volume running 5x normal means somebody is betting hard that rates are about to come down, which lines up with the growing pressure on the Fed from the White House and the softer economic data we've been seeing. The rotation into Utilities and Energy alongside REITs tells me institutions are positioning for a "lower rates plus energy dominance" playbook, likely anticipating continued deregulation, LNG export expansion, and the permitting reform tucked into recent legislation. On the flip side, the smart money is quietly running for the exits in Consumer Discretionary (4x volume, P/C over 2) and Industrials — this is the tariff trade in reverse, where traders are betting that tariff pass-through costs and stretched consumers finally crack retail earnings, while Industrials get hit by retaliatory measures and slowing capex. The Healthcare bearishness is almost certainly about drug pricing executive orders and Medicare negotiation expansion that isn't getting front-page coverage but is very real in Washington. What jumps out as contradictory: Tech shows bullish signals even as Communication Services (which houses Google and Meta) is being hedged aggressively — that split suggests antitrust and AI regulation fears are being isolated to the ad-driven mega caps rather than semis and infrastructure. The non-obvious tell is the credit market: high-yield is being hedged bearishly while investment-grade gets bought, and spreads are widening — that combination usually precedes a growth scare within 4-8 weeks, so the "bullish" defensive sectors (REITs, Utilities) aren't really a risk-on trade, they're a stealth recession hedge dressed up as a rate-cut bet. Watch for a headline-driven wobble in the next month
